The fit gives Dq ≈ 1845 cm⁻¹ and B ≈ 727 cm⁻¹ for [Co(H₂O)₆]³⁺ with C/B = 4.5. I got this by fitting the two bands as the low-spin d⁶ spin-allowed transitions from the ¹A₁g ground state, using the Tanabe–Sugano fit tool.

**Assignments:** 16 474 cm⁻¹ is ¹A₁g → ¹T₁g and 25 381 cm⁻¹ is ¹A₁g → ¹T₂g.

**Fits at fixed C:** the tool needs an absolute C, so I ran it at three values and then found the C that satisfies C = 4.5B.

| C (cm⁻¹) | Fitted Dq (cm⁻¹) | Fitted B (cm⁻¹) |
|---|---|---|
| 2900 | 1823.5 | 723.1 |
| 3100 | 1835.1 | 725.3 |
| 3300 | 1846.5 | 727.5 |

B changes by only about 0.011 cm⁻¹ per cm⁻¹ of C. C = 3272 cm⁻¹ is self-consistent, because 3272 / 4.5 ≈ 727. At that point Dq ≈ 1845 cm⁻¹, so 10Dq ≈ 18 450 cm⁻¹.

**Caveat:** two bands fix two parameters exactly, so there is no check on fit quality. The result depends on the assumed C/B and on the band assignments.

**Result:** Dq ≈ 1845 cm⁻¹, B ≈ 727 cm⁻¹ (C ≈ 3272 cm⁻¹). B is about 67% of the free-ion value for Co³⁺, which I took from memory (roughly 1100 cm⁻¹) and did not check with the nephelauxetic tool.
